text:
maria: Hey team — noticed a steady connection/FD growth in our long-running sample app using the python SDK. After ~12h the process gets almost no free sockets and starts timing out.

maria: Repro steps: start the async worker (uvicorn + fastapi), run workload that calls Redwood client at ~20 rps, let it run. After ~10-12h failures ramp.

maria: Logs show a lot of `ResourceWarning: unclosed` coming from `httpx._client` and then `Too many open files` errors. Minimal stack:

maria: ```
async with RedwoodClient(api_key=...) as c:
    await c.generate(...)
# but the service keeps spawning tasks and sometimes doesn't await client.shutdown()
```

alex: ugh. Is this the `HTTPX` connpool we saw earlier or something SDK-specific?

maria: looks like interactions between our `Client` session lifetime and app-level worker restart cycles. The SDK claims to use a global async client, but in the sample app we create a client per request (bad pattern). However even when switching to a single client per worker, fd count still creeps.

tim: can you paste a small heap/FD snapshot? also the version of `redwood-sdk` and `httpx`?

maria: sdk 0.7.4, httpx 0.25.0. FD dump attached (trimmed):

maria: ```
FD  TCP  10.0.0.1:443 -> 52.54.12.1:52344  ESTABLISHED
FD  TCP  10.0.0.1:443 -> 52.54.12.1:52345  TIME_WAIT
... many half-closed sockets ...
```

sara: if you can reproduce locally, try setting `pool_limits` on the httpx transport and enabling `httpx.AsyncClient(limits=...)` to see if that caps growth. But SDK should expose a knob if we manage sockets internally.

maria: yeah — I tried `limits = httpx.Limits(max_keepalive_connections=10, max_connections=100)` manually and growth slowed but didn't stop. Also saw `asyncio.Task` objects piling up in `asyncio.Task.all_tasks()` with `Client.request` frames.

alex: sounds like two issues: (1) tasks not awaited on shutdown; (2) transport/connection reuse bug where connections aren't reused properly and leak.

tim: can you try running with `GC debug` and `PYTHONASYNCIODEBUG=1`? would help see unhandled cancelled tasks. Also curious if TLS context or verify toggles cause sockets to not be pooled.

maria: will run a short run with those flags and report back. Also added a small patch on my fork to explicitly call `await transport.close()` in our client's `__aexit__` to force-close connections — that temporarily solved it locally.

sara: good temporary workaround. We should add a public `client.close()` / `await client.aclose()` doc example and ensure SDK's context manager does the same. SDK should also accept `transport_limits` param.

alex: filing a tracking ticket for SDK: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/342 (internal link) — placeholder: "python SDK: ensure clean shutdown + expose connection limits for AsyncClient"

maria: noted. creating a minimal repro gist and will attach to the issue. Will also try newer httpx (0.26.x) to rule out transport bug.

tim: thanks. if you can include a tiny harness that spawns many short-lived tasks hitting client.generate(), that would help. we might have to add a `weakref` finalizer for client instances as a last resort.

deploy-bot: CI build redwood-sdk@pr-678 succeeded — tests include newly added shutdown test (flaky, rerun recommended).

maria: quick follow-up — the transient mitigation we use in our sample app: keep a global `RedwoodClient.instance()` per worker and call `atexit.register(lambda: asyncio.get_event_loop().run_until_complete(client.aclose()))`. Not ideal but better than FD death.

sara: let's add a short note in the devex sample apps about client lifetime (async context manager recommended, single client per process/worker, call aclose() on shutdown). I'll open a docs PR.

alex: created PR #701 on SDK to add `limits` passthrough and explicit `transport.close()` in `__aexit__`. reviewers: @tim @sara.

maria: thanks — once PR lands I'll rerun long-run tests for 48h.

tim: great. Also add a regression test that runs the sample app for a few minutes with synthetic connections to catch fd growth early in CI.

maria: agreed. I'll add a small CI job that runs for 10 minutes and fails if FD growth > 50 from baseline.

sara: :thumbsup: thanks for the detailed repro and for filing the issue.

alex: keeping this open until we ship the fix & the docs update.

maria: ending note — if anyone else hits similar flakiness in customer infra, ping me and I'll share the temporary workaround.
